chapter: Erroll Garner and the Los Angeles scene
title: The marijuana bust and the honor farm with Garner
summary: Both were set up with joints and sent to an honor farm, forbidden to play together.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and the Prohibition-era clubs

blocks.x: But evidently... I don't know why they did this. But I think they set me and Garner up, because a guy that had been hanging out with us all the the time... You know, like, we were smoking pot. So he'd come by... One night he came by, and just as I was going out the door, he gave me a stick of reefer, you know. So I just put it in my pocket, because I

figured, what the heck,, I don't feel like smoking it right now, I'll wait until I can drive off somewhere. So I kept it. And then Erroll said they did the same thing to him; on his way out, some cat walked up to him and handed him a joint -- and he took it, too, you know. And he got popped and I got popped on the same night. In fact, on the day of the trial, they sent us both up to an honor farm up in Los Angeles.
Is that like a work farm?

Yeah. You go out and you do light work to kill the time. Like, I had a job passing out bread. You know, two slices of bread here and one there, and so forth and so on. Which was all right. I mean, I didn't mind, because I... The only thing was that they wouldn't let us practice together. They wouldn't let Erroll and I play together. He could play in the morning and I could play in the afternoon, or I could play in the morning and he could play in the afternoon. But whichever one decided they wanted to go out first, that's the way the situation was.
They wouldn't let you get together.
No, they wouldn't let us play together. But finally, when we got out, then we got together, because we

talked and laughed and kidded about being up at the honor farm. As if they thought they had done a great, big, magnificent thing, and all they did was just made me develop my friendship with Erroll Garner. Because really, that's the way it was.
